questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The ulcer has indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are non-tender and rubbery. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The classic Hunterian chancre of primary syphilis is a single, painless, indurated ulcer with a clean base and non-tender regional lymphadenopathy (Treponema pallidum). Chancroid is painful; herpes presents with multiple vesicles/ulcers; LGV causes a transient papule then inguinal buboes.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman from rural India has a single hypopigmented patch on the back with diminished sensation. Slit-skin smear shows no AFB. Nerve function is normal. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Single-lesion paucibacillary leprosy is treated with a single dose ROM regimen — Rifampicin 600 mg + Ofloxacin 400 mg + Minocycline 100 mg. PB-MDT (6 months) is for 2–5 lesions; MB-MDT is for >5 lesions or positive smear.

questions.q: A 45-year-old immunocompetent patient develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along a thoracic dermatomal distribution with burning pain. The most feared complication in this age group is:
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) — pain persisting >3 months after rash healing — is the most common and feared complication of herpes zoster, especially in patients over 50. Antiviral therapy started within 72 h reduces PHN risk.

questions.q: A 25-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 80/mm³) has widespread flesh-coloured umbilicated papules on the face and trunk. Histology shows large intracytoplasmic inclusions pushing the nucleus to the periphery. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (Molluscipoxvirus) produces Henderson-Paterson bodies — large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions that compress the nucleus peripherally. Disseminated, giant molluscum is a marker of severe immunosuppression (CD4 <100).

questions.q: A 3-year-old child has superficial erosions with honey-coloured crusting around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The first-line topical treatment for localised disease is:
questions.exp: Impetigo is caused predominantly by S. aureus. Topical mupirocin 2% is the first-line agent for localised non-bullous impetigo with high efficacy. Fusidic acid is an alternative; neomycin has a higher sensitisation rate. Oral antibiotics are used for widespread disease.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male has well-defined, scaly, erythematous plaques on the scalp and extensor surfaces. Auspitz sign is positive. Which cytokine is most central to the pathogenesis?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is predominantly Th17-mediated; IL-17A is the key effector cytokine driving keratinocyte proliferation and neutrophil recruitment. Biologics targeting IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab) and its upstream driver IL-23 are highly effective for moderate-to-severe psoriasis.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child has scaling, pruritic patches on the scalp with broken hair shafts and cervical lymphadenopathy. Wood's lamp shows bright green fluorescence. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix infection and characteristically shows bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. T. tonsurans (endothrix) does not fluoresce and is more prevalent in adults in some endemic areas. E. floccosum does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has tense bullae on urticarial and normal-appearing skin. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 along the BMZ. The autoantigen targeted is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is caused by IgG autoantibodies against BP180 (NC16A domain) and BP230, both hemidesmosomal proteins. Linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ is the DIF hallmark. Desmoglein 3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris; type VII collagen in EBA.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with flaccid blisters and erosions involving the oral mucosa followed by skin involvement. Nikolsky sign is positive. The characteristic histopathological finding is:
opts: Suprabasal acantholysis with tombstone appearance of basal cells
Dermal neutrophilic infiltrate with papillary oedema
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris shows suprabasal acantholysis — loss of cohesion above the basal layer, leaving a single row of basal cells attached to the BMZ like 'tombstones'. The blister forms just above the basal layer due to anti-Dsg3 (and Dsg1) antibodies.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on WHO-MDT develops sudden fever, evanescent erythematous tender nodules, and joint pain. Nerve function remains intact. The drug of choice for this reaction is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 reaction) in LL/BL leprosy is best treated with thalidomide (anti-TNF-alpha), the drug of choice for recurrent or resistant ENL. Prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated (e.g., women of childbearing age). Clofazimine is used for long-term suppression.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman has malar erythema, oral ulcers, and photosensitivity. ANA is positive at 1:320. Anti-dsDNA is elevated. Which antibody is most specific for this diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies are highly specific (~99%) for SLE, though sensitivity is low (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is both sensitive and specific for SLE and correlates with disease activity and lupus nephritis. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman has symmetric proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, and Gottron's papules. CK is 3000 U/L. The investigation most useful for monitoring disease activity is:
questions.exp: Serum CK is the most sensitive and commonly used marker for monitoring disease activity and treatment response in dermatomyositis/polymyositis. It correlates with muscle inflammation. Anti-Jo-1 indicates antisynthetase syndrome and interstitial lung disease risk.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman has skin thickening on fingers extending to forearms, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. ANA shows an anti-centromere pattern. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody is characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome). Diffuse cutaneous SSc is associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I). MCTD is associated with anti-U1-RNP antibodies. Morphoea is localised and not associated with these antibodies.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with painless superficial inguinal lymphadenopathy after a transient genital papule. Frei test is positive. The causative organism belongs to which Chlamydia serovars?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3, which are more invasive than serovars D–K (non-invasive genital infections). Serovars A, B, Ba cause trachoma. The Frei test is now obsolete but was historically positive in LGV.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive patient has painful perianal ulcers. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The most appropriate treatment regimen is:
opts: Oral acyclovir 400 mg 5 times/day for 10 days
questions.exp: Herpes simplex in immunocompromised (HIV, CD4 <200) patients with severe or extensive disease requires IV acyclovir (5 mg/kg 8-hourly) due to the risk of visceral dissemination. Oral antivirals are reserved for mild disease or suppression. Duration is usually 7–10 days.

questions.q: A 45-year-old presents with recurrent furunculosis. Bacterial culture yields MRSA. The best oral antibiotic for community-acquired MRSA skin infection is:
questions.exp: Co-trimoxazole (TMP-SMX) is the oral drug of choice for community-acquired MRSA (CA-MRSA) skin and soft-tissue infections. Doxycycline and clindamycin are alternatives. Standard beta-lactams (amoxicillin, cephalexin) are ineffective against MRSA.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with a solitary, well-defined erythematous plaque on the forearm with central hypopigmentation and a raised edge. Sensation is reduced within the patch. Nerve biopsy shows granulomas in the perineurium. The Ridley-Jopling classification is:
questions.exp: Borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy presents with few asymmetric plaques, well-defined outer edges, moderately impaired sensation, and perineural granulomas. TT has a single lesion with complete sensory loss; BB has many lesions with Swiss-cheese appearance; LL has diffuse infiltration without sensory loss.

questions.q: A neonate develops flaccid blistering within 24 hours of birth. The mother has circulating anti-desmoglein antibodies. The condition resolves in weeks. This is:
questions.exp: Neonatal pemphigus results from transplacental passage of maternal IgG anti-desmoglein antibodies (Dsg1/Dsg3). Blistering is transient, resolving as maternal antibodies clear. SSSS is due to staphylococcal exfoliatin toxin; EBS is due to keratin gene mutations.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man has a pearly, translucent papule on the nose with telangiectasias and central ulceration following prolonged sun exposure. The best treatment is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) in a high-risk location (nose, periocular, lips, ears) is best managed with Mohs micrographic surgery, providing >99% cure rate and maximal tissue conservation. Cryotherapy and topical agents are reserved for low-risk superficial BCCs. PDT is for superficial BCCs only.

questions.q: A 55-year-old farmer presents with a rapidly growing keratotic nodule on the dorsum of the hand over 6 weeks, with a central keratin-filled crater. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous proliferation with horn pearls. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) is a rapidly growing keratinocyte tumour with a central keratin-filled crater appearing over 6–8 weeks in sun-exposed areas. It may spontaneously regress. Due to its histological resemblance to well-differentiated SCC, many treat it as low-grade SCC.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman has multiple asymptomatic skin-coloured papules on her lower eyelids bilaterally. Histology shows dilated cystic ducts lined by a double layer of flat epithelial cells. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Syringomas are benign eccrine sweat duct tumours presenting as small skin-coloured to yellowish papules on the lower eyelids of middle-aged women. Histology shows comma-shaped ('tadpole') ducts lined by two cuboidal cell layers. Xanthelasma shows lipid-laden macrophages; milia are keratin-filled cysts.

questions.q: A 30-year-old has a 2 cm dark-brown pigmented lesion on the upper back. Dermoscopy shows an irregular network, atypical dots/globules, and regression structures. The most appropriate next step is:
questions.exp: For suspected melanoma, excisional biopsy with narrow (1–2 mm) margins is the gold standard to obtain the entire lesion for Breslow thickness measurement and complete histopathological staging. Punch or shave biopsies may miss the deepest component; imiquimod is not appropriate for suspected melanoma.

questions.q: At 48 hours of patch testing, a test site shows erythema, infiltration, and vesicles. At 96 hours the reaction has intensified further. This crescendo pattern indicates:
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis (Type IV delayed hypersensitivity) on patch testing shows a crescendo pattern — reaction intensifies from 48 h to 96 h. Irritant reactions peak at 48 h and then fade (decrescendo). Vesiculation further supports ACD rather than irritant reaction.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with chronic flexural eczema since childhood also has asthma and allergic rhinitis. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. The most common allergen detected on skin prick testing is:
questions.exp: House dust mite (HDM) — particularly Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus — is the most common sensitising aeroallergen in atopic dermatitis worldwide, identified in 60–80% of AD patients. Reducing HDM exposure can meaningfully improve AD control.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman has multiple hypopigmented macules on the face and trunk. Wood's lamp shows chalk-white fluorescence. KOH mount shows short curved hyphae and round spores. The drug of choice for widespread disease is:
opts: Oral itraconazole 200 mg OD for 5–7 days
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur) shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' on KOH (short hyphae and round spores). Oral itraconazole 200 mg OD for 5–7 days is highly effective for widespread disease. Topical agents (selenium sulfide, ketoconazole shampoo) are used for limited disease. Griseofulvin is inactive against Malassezia.

questions.q: A 35-year-old diabetic presents with rapidly spreading erythema, oedema, and necrosis of the scrotum and perineum with crepitus. The most critical immediate management step is:
opts: Urgent surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum antibiotics
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a polymicrobial necrotising fasciitis of the perineum/genitalia with high mortality. Urgent surgical debridement is life-saving and must not be delayed for imaging. Broad-spectrum antibiotics covering anaerobes, Gram-negative, and Gram-positive organisms are adjunctive.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman is 16 weeks pregnant with worsening facial melasma. The most appropriate topical treatment is:
questions.exp: Azelaic acid (FDA Category B) is safe in pregnancy and is the preferred topical agent for melasma, working by inhibiting tyrosinase. Hydroquinone is Category C (avoid); tretinoin is Category X (teratogenic); aggressive chemical peels are contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.q: A 15-year-old has Blaschko-linear hypopigmented streaks on the trunk since infancy with no systemic abnormalities. Wood's lamp enhances the hypopigmentation. Biopsy shows normal melanocyte number but reduced melanin transfer. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Nevus depigmentosus (achromic nevus) presents as stable hypopigmented patches following Blaschko lines since birth, with reduced melanin transfer but normal melanocyte numbers. Hypomelanosis of Ito is associated with systemic abnormalities (CNS, MSK). Vitiligo shows melanocyte absence.

questions.q: Which drug used in dermatology requires G6PD testing before initiation due to risk of haemolytic anaemia?
questions.exp: Dapsone can cause dose-dependent methaemoglobinaemia and haemolytic anaemia, which is severely exacerbated in G6PD-deficient patients. G6PD levels must be checked before initiation. Dapsone is used in leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis, bullous pemphigoid, and other conditions.

questions.q: A 17-year-old boy with severe nodulo-cystic acne is started on isotretinoin. Which monitoring parameter is most important to repeat at 4–6 weeks after starting treatment?
opts: Fasting lipids and liver function tests
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause hypertriglyceridaemia (risk of pancreatitis) and elevated transaminases. Fasting lipid profile and LFTs must be checked at baseline and repeated at 4–6 weeks, then every 1–3 months. CBC and TFTs are not routinely required during isotretinoin therapy.

questions.q: On dermoscopy, 'leaf-like areas' (brown-grey leaf-like structures at the periphery) are most characteristic of which tumour?
questions.exp: Leaf-like areas (also called leaf-like structures) on dermoscopy are a highly specific feature of pigmented basal cell carcinoma. Other BCC-specific dermoscopic structures include spoke-wheel areas, arborising telangiectasias, large blue-grey ovoid nests, and multiple blue-grey globules.
